rules.r: In a follow-up submission, any service you remove is treated as cancelled. Keep every service on the approval so it can be processed at claim level.
Services sent with uncontracted codes are rejected. Follow the network protocol and submit new service codes three months in advance for analysis and feedback.
Emergency: no pre-authorisation before admitting the member — but the request must reach the payer within 24 hours of the patient's arrival in the emergency department.

If the eligibility response says no pre-authorisation is required, outpatient services are exempt regardless of cost or type — but inpatient admissions and every sub-limit benefit still need it: optical, dental, hearing aids, dialysis, autism, psychiatry, Alzheimer, circumcision, ear piercing, and maternity under the antenatal protocol.
The pre-authorisation threshold is shown in the eligibility response and is calculated on gross service prices per visit, excluding the consultation fee. Medication carries a separate sub-limit.
Inpatient extensions stay under the same approval reference. On the first day of a new month, submit a new approval number.
Daily progress notes are required for inpatient extensions.
Dental: request only the treatment that can be delivered in one appointment. Do not request the later stages in advance.
Dental: tooth number, attachments and radiographs are what allow an automated approval.
Dispensing a sunglasses frame and swapping the lenses for medical ones is recorded as fraud.
Chronic medication is submitted for 3 months, or up to the policy expiry date, whichever comes first.
Only standard devices with standard agreed pricing may be submitted.
Visit visa requests: the correct EMR form is required, the passport number or identifier must be entered in capitals, and every service needs prior authorisation.
Domestic helper requests: every service needs prior authorisation.
Post-assisted-pregnancy and IVF care is covered for CHI policies.
Normal delivery and caesarean section are covered where the caesarean is medically justified.
Once a pregnancy is complicated, every visit needs its own pre-authorisation — the protocol exemption no longer applies.
Aramco and SABIC accounts follow their own protocols; the Bupa protocol does not apply to them.

If the eligibility check shows no pre-authorisation is required, Bupa still requires it for every sub-limit benefit (optical, dental, hearing aids, dialysis, autism, psychiatry, Alzheimer, circumcision, ear piercing), the first maternity visit under the antenatal protocol, home health care, the listed medications, CPAP and BiPAP, insulin pumps, and the listed inpatient services.
The medication list applies to direct-access, referral and walk-in prescriptions alike.
Admission extension needs a request where the hospital is not covered by a Bupa roving doctor.
Emergency: when the patient is not eligible, submit the case through the EMR request type under the emergency protocol.
Dental: the ICD-10 code must match the requested services and follow ADA and the SBS circular — version 2 for Tawuniya, version 3 for Al Rajhi.
Hearing aids are approved only through a hearing-aid provider, and the optical benefit only through an optical shop.
Trauma: state how, when and where it happened and whether it is work related; for sport, whether the patient is a professional player.
Road traffic accidents: attach the police report and the guarantee letter — filled out by the member for Al Rajhi; signed by the patient for Tawuniya when the patient is not 100% responsible.

Normal lenses must already include blue light reduction, UV protection, anti-reflective and scratch-resistant coatings at no extra cost; tinted, photochromic, polarised and transition lenses, ready-made reading glasses and cosmetic contact lenses are not covered.
Uncovered optical extras: Al Rajhi lets the patient add them for cash; Tawuniya does not allow it, even for cash.
Glasses with a sphere of 0.25 dioptre or less and no cylinder above 0.25 DC are not dispensed; the optical prescription must be uploaded, clear, and carry the examiner's stamp.

Biologics are refused most often for: missing disease-severity documentation, missing initial investigations, no evidence of step-therapy failure, missing TB, HBV or HCV screening, missing specialist assessment, and an insufficient rationale for the biologic chosen.

Specialised infant formula: breastfeeding first. Cow's milk allergy — extensively hydrolysed formula for 4–8 weeks, continued 4–6 months if it works. Lactose intolerance — non-persistent diarrhoea stays on breastfeeding; diarrhoea over 14 days in a formula-fed child gets lactose-free formula for 4–6 weeks, then a paediatric gastroenterologist if there is no improvement.

The Minimum Data Set is signed by Tawuniya's medical director and the provider's medical director. Submitting it complete the first time is meant to cut waiting time, avoid refusals for missing information and remove requests for further information.

Bupa's Prerequisites document prints ICD-10-CM codes, while Saudi claims are coded in ICD-10-AM. 68 of its 151 sets print codes that do not exist in ICD-10-AM or point at a different condition — see Code issues.
